uncited: Brick-based structures replace the variable-resolution hierarchical subdivision of sparse voxel octrees with fixed-size cubic blocks ("bricks") to optimize for hardware-friendly memory access and parallel construction [11886-sparse-voxel-brick-set].

They solve the traversal complexity and shader divergence of recursive tree structures by enabling branch-free, linear memory access patterns suitable for real-time ray tracing and GPU cache coherency [21177-brick-map].
The family shares the mechanism of partitioning the 3D domain into fixed-granularity cubic blocks rather than recursive nodes [11886-sparse-voxel-brick-set].
These blocks are stored in a sparse container (e.g., a low-resolution grid or hash map) that maps spatial regions to brick data [21177-brick-map].
This approach prioritizes uniform granularity to balance memory usage and traversal speed, specifically optimizing for hardware interpolation and parallel processing [11886-sparse-voxel-brick-set].
